item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is substantially more mergeable because it implements the requested convenience API with the established multipart helper and keeps the change focused. It still needs revision to delegate through FilesService.Add and to add the required streamed-reader and reader-error tests.","reasons":["B reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile exactly as required, producing the intended replayable buffered body.","B preserves the existing FilesOption model and avoids unrelated retry-transport changes.","A explicitly violates the contract by adding association form fields and WithFilesFormFields, extending the multipart helper, and refactoring Raw.Do retry and body-ownership semantics.","Both implementations duplicate Add's request, response, and error handling by calling Raw.Do directly instead of routing through FilesService.Add; in B this is a small, localized correction, while A compounds it with duplicate machinery and broader API changes."],"risks_a":["Adds association fields despite the explicit prohibition.","Changes generic retry behavior and ownership/closing semantics for seekable request bodies, well outside scope.","Uses NewFileWithFields rather than the required established NewFile path and duplicates Add logic in Upload of calling Add directly instead of delegating to it directly though says route encoded body through existing Add."],"risks_b":["Upload calls Raw.Do directly instead of FilesService.Add, risking future divergence in option handling and error semantics.","Retry coverage uses bytes.NewReader rather than genuinely streamed content, so it does not prove buffering makes a non-replayable source retryable.","No test verifies propagation of source-reader failures, and the combined validation error is less precise than separate filename/content errors."]}
